children: New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has issued notice on a contempt application filed by Gillette India Limited against Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt Ltd, in proceedings concerning an advertisement alleged to be disparaging of Gillette.

The application was moved under Order XXXIX Rule 2-A read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, by Gillette alleging violation of an undertaking given before the Court by Bombay Shaving Company in relation to the original advertisement.

Gillette India submitted that despite the undertaking given by Bombay Shaving Company to take down the original advertisement, the Defendant had released a purportedly revised version which contained essentially the same offending content.

The Defendant disputed the allegations, submitting that the revised advertisement was a reworked version of the original advertisement and did not contain the allegedly offending portions or disparage the Plaintiff in law.

Importantly, upon a prima-facie viewing of the revised advertisement, the Court observed that there was “no perceptible difference in the impact” of the revised advertisement as compared to the original advertisement.

The Court has accordingly issued notice on the contempt application filed by Gillette and directed that Bombay Shaving Company shall not run the revised advertisement until the next date of hearing. The matter has been listed for 5 October 2026.

Gillette India Limited was represented by Senior Advocate Chander M. Lall, instructed by the team of Aerion Legal including Ankur Sangal, Pragya Mishra, Saumya Bajpai, Yashodhara Raina, A. Mehar and Swastik Sant.
Bombay Shaving Company was represented by Tanya Varma, Prithvi Singh, Vardaan Anand, Ruchika Yadav.
